modify.note: In the booker DatePicker, make the automatic month advance depend on availability in the month being displayed. The CRM-owner lookup can return slots from the following month, so deriving one list of nonempty days from the whole response incorrectly makes an empty current month look bookable. Restrict the dates used for this decision to the browsing month and year, using the existing nonempty-schedule-day logic. Keep the existing restriction that automatic advancement applies to the current month. Wait for a completed availability response before deciding that the month is empty; missing data or an in-progress fetch should not trigger navigation. When the loaded current month has no bookable days, advance through the existing month-change callback so the selected date and day-count state stay consistent. A bookable day in the displayed month must prevent advancement even when the response spans multiple months. Decouple the booker DatePicker from the schedule-query object by accepting `slots` and `isLoading` directly, and update callers. Add the shared `Slots` type.

In the calendar DatePicker, keep the actual slot data available for rendering and out-of-office information, and use `isLoading` consistently. Expose the named `DatePicker` export and the month label's `<time>` element with its machine-readable `dateTime` value.

add_edges.label: renders calendar DatePicker
add_edges.note: The booker DatePicker renders the calendar DatePicker.
